text:
emma c.: hey everyone, excited to start! i'm blocked on the Okta / Google SSO stuff. i signed in to redwood.okta.com but when i try to enroll Okta Verify it says 'No enrollment token'. Google redirects me to pick an account and then says 'Access denied'. didn't get a 1Password invite either. any quick wins?
it-support: welcome emma! common culprits: (1) your account wasn't in the provisioning group yet, (2) the Okta invite expired, or (3) browser/account chooser is picking a personal google account. can you confirm emma.c@redwood.com and whether you clicked the onboarding email within 24h? also try incognito.
emma c.: yes it's emma.c@redwood.com. clicked the email earlier today. tried incognito and still 'No enrollment token'. screenshot text: `Enrollment failed (E_NO_TOKEN)`.
infra-admin: checking SCIM now. looks like your user was created but missed the "employees" group due to a provisioning race. i've added you to the group and resent the Google Workspace + 1Password (SSO) invites. also forced an Okta factor reset so a fresh QR should appear.
mike: fwiw when my invite acted weird i had to sign out of my personal google account in the browser otherwise the SSO flow picked the wrong account. if you're using Chrome profiles it helps to switch to a fresh profile.
it-support: admin did the reset. after you sign into redwood.okta.com you should see a prompt to "Set up an authenticator app" with a QR. if the QR still doesn't show, try a different browser or temporarily disable privacy extensions.
emma c.: okay i opened a clean chrome profile, went to redwood.okta.com and the QR appeared. scanned in Okta Verify but the app shows 'Time skew detected' when i try the test push.
security: time skew is usually the device clock. On iOS/Android set Date & Time -> Automatic. if that doesn't fix it, uninstall/reinstall Okta Verify.
emma c.: toggled automatic time, reinstalled Okta Verify, push worked and i'm in. Google SSO still initially failed until i clicked the new 1Password invite link  the first link went to a "create password" page.
it-support: that means the original invite wasn't SSO-enforced. i reissued an SSO-only 1Password invite to emma.c@redwood.com. click "Sign in with Okta" on the invite page and it will use your existing session. docs: https://redwood.example.com/internal/onboarding/1password-sso
emma c.: the SSO invite worked, accepted via Okta. quick question: 1Password asked me to register a device key (WebAuthn) and suggested adding a security key; do we require hardware keys?
security: we encourage hardware keys but they're optional. we require at least one strong factor (Okta Verify + recovery codes). If you add a YubiKey, file it as a second factor in 1Password and consider adding a second backup method. See policy: https://redwood.example.com/internal/security/mfa-policy
emma c.: noted. one more tiny issue: after accepting 1Password SSO it prompted for a master-password fallback. i didn't set one and it accepted SSO. should i have created that password?
it-support: no need if you used "Sign in with Okta"  SSO is primary. If you ever see an explicit create-password flow, open a ticket and we'll reissue an SSO-enforced invite. store Okta recovery codes in your personal 1Password vault.
onboarding-bot: Welcome to Redwood, emma! :tada: Checklist updated: Okta MFA enrolled, Google Workspace access confirmed, 1Password SSO accepted. Join #new-hires lunch at 12pm.
emma c.: all green now, thanks everyone! ping me if you want to grab coffee later :coffee:
